nora_sre: Heads-up: Rapid AZ failover drill + SLO guardrail tweak planned Sun 2026-05-02 05:00-06:00 UTC. Goal: validate automated preemption, routing preemption, and SLO rollback behavior under simulated AZ loss. Affects: us-east and eu-west control + edge planes.
nora_sre: TL;DR flow: failover canary (single AZ -> standby pool) -> observe 15m -> if stable ramp to multi-AZ failover simulation -> measure SLO triggers and automatic rollback. We'll enable shorter circuit-breaker dwell during the drill to trigger guardrails quickly.
opsbot: Scheduled event: "rapid-az-failover-drill" 2026-05-02T05:00:00Z created by nora_sre (ops link: https://ops.internal/events/2026-failover-drill).
josh_oncall: Ack. I'll be oncall that window and watching infer.p95, route.error_rate, route.fallback_rate, and routing.preemptions.
meera_prod: Product: do we need customer comms for Dedicated? We should have support blurb ready if any tenant sees >8% p95 increase for >20m.
nora_sre: Agreed. Only send if sustained breach. Template: short outage note + mitigation steps + ETA. I'll drop it to Support before the window.
alvin_eng: Quick Q: what exact guardrail changes are we testing?
nora_sre: We're shortening the SLO rollback trigger dwell from 30m -> 10m and enabling preemption ramp-down to 0% within 90s if error spike detected. Also enabling rapid route fallback to 'fallback-model-pool' when route_error_rate > 0.4% absolute.
alvin_eng: Nice. Which flags to flip during the test?
nora_sre: Ops flags: `routing.preemption.enabled=true`, `slo.rollback.dwell=600` (seconds), `slo.rollback.multiplier=1.12` (p95 threshold), `routing.fallback_pool=fallback-model-pool`. Commands below.
nora_sre: Runbook excerpt (short):
```
# start canary failover
infractl failover start --az us-east-1b --mode canary --percent 5
# observe for 15m
# ramp
infractl failover ramp --target-percent 50 --stages 25,50
# rollback
infractl failover abort --az us-east-1b
# quick toggle guardrail
infractl config set routing.preemption.enabled=true
infractl config set slo.rollback.dwell=600
```
josh_oncall: Rollback criteria I want on the runbook: infer.p95 > baseline*1.18 for 10m OR 5xx_rate increase of +0.5% absolute for 5m. Also watch route.fallback_rate; if >15% persistent -> rollback.
telemetry_bot: Alert rule created: failover-drill-watch (metrics: infer.p95, route.5xx_pct, route.fallback_rate) thresholds configured.
meera_prod: We'll prep support notice and a short changelog entry for internal customers. If a Dedicated tenant is impacted include tenant id, affected routes, and observed p95.
alvin_eng: For canary observers: I'll provide a small synthetic load generator hitting token-heavy routes to exercise preemption. Will cap per-AZ QPS at 200 and add jitter.
josh_oncall: I'll run the failover canary command and keep the sequence in the incident page. I'll post status updates here at start, +15m, +40m, and completion.
nora_sre: Important: during the drill we want to see the quick rollback behave. The 'circuit-breaker dwell' will be 90s so preemption should flip fast. Note: this is a simulation; we won't remove traffic from physical AZs, only route-level preemption.
alvin_eng: Where's the incident/runbook?
nora_sre: Runbook + preflight checklist: https://confluence.internal/ops/rapid-az-failover-drill. Incident page: https://incident.internal/INC-2026-FAILDRILL.
opsbot: Config queued: failover-drill@infra 2026-05-02T05:00Z by nora_sre.
josh_oncall: Preflight checks I'll run at 04:15 UTC: 1) alerting working 2) synthetic load script smoke 3) telemetry dashboards show baselines. Will paste checklist here.
meera_prod: Remind: if we see Dedicated customer impact, cc support@redwood-inference and product-incident@redwood-inference.
nora_sre: Thanks all. If you want to shadow the canary ping me by 04:45 UTC. We'll keep the window tight and attempt to validate rollback speed rather than induce long outages.
